content.body:
Roadmap for the enhancement packages and current backlog.

## Recommended Implementation Order
1. Architecture decomposition and tool lifecycle standardization (#79)
2. Security, audit trail, and dependency hardening (#80)
3. UI/UX system and accessibility modernization (#81)
4. Performance and startup-path optimization (#82)
5. Error handling and observability consolidation (#83)
6. Test infrastructure and quality gates (#84)

## Current backlog grouping
- UI / preferences / documentation flow items: issues #8-78
- Package-level architecture work: issue #79
- Security hardening: issue #80
- UI/UX modernization: issue #81
- Performance work: issue #82
- Observability work: issue #83
- Testing and quality gates: issue #84

## Notes
- The order above is risk-first: reduce structural and security risk before broad UI and performance work.
- Test and quality-gate work should close the loop before the roadmap is considered complete.

content.body:
Package goal: make regression detection cheaper by organizing tests around modules and enforcing clear quality gates.

Why this package matters:
- The repo already has substantial validation coverage, but the test layout should scale with the number of tools and shared modules.
- Packages with UI, startup, security, and performance changes need focused fixtures and smoke tests so refactors stay safe.
- Coverage, linting, typing, and performance checks should all be tied to the affected code paths.

Implementation items:
- Introduce reusable fixtures for hub, tool, theme, and preference tests.
- Group tests by module boundary so new behavior lands with a nearby test surface.
- Add lightweight performance and startup checks to catch regressions early.
- Keep CI gates aligned with the package boundaries so each future enhancement package can be validated independently.

Representative files:
- [tests](tests)
- [pytest.ini](pytest.ini)
- [setup.cfg](setup.cfg)
- [scripts](scripts)

content.body:
Package goal: unify how errors are captured, reported, and logged across GUI, service, and background contexts.

Why this package matters:
- [core/error_handler.py](core/error_handler.py) is already a compatibility layer, which suggests the real implementation boundary has shifted and needs a cleaner contract.
- Startup logging in [main.py](main.py) is direct and local, while other areas likely use their own logging patterns.
- Multiple logging paths make diagnosis harder and increase the chance of inconsistent user feedback.

Implementation items:
- Consolidate logging and error context into one shared abstraction with consistent severity and metadata fields.
- Separate user-facing error presentation from telemetry/logging so failures are both understandable and traceable.
- Add structured context for tool launches, file operations, and background failures.
- Reduce duplicate logging entry points and standardize fallback behavior when optional subsystems fail.

Representative files:
- [core/error_handler.py](core/error_handler.py)
- [src/core](src/core)
- [main.py](main.py)
- [gui/common](gui/common)

content.body:
Package goal: reduce startup latency and avoid paying the cost of optional features until the user actually needs them.

Why this package matters:
- [main.py](main.py) initializes database state and feature detection during import-time startup, which increases launch cost and failure surface.
- Optional features such as PDF tooling and explorer variants should not slow down the default path when they are unavailable or unused.
- Several workflows likely benefit from deferred imports and narrower initialization boundaries.

Implementation items:
- Lazy-load heavyweight subsystems and move expensive initialization out of import-time code.
- Measure startup time, first-window time, and optional-feature load cost before and after changes.
- Make optional integrations fail soft and only load when selected by the user.
- Add small performance benchmarks for the high-cost workflows so regressions are visible.

Representative files:
- [main.py](main.py)
- [src/tools/pdf_tools](src/tools/pdf_tools)
- [scripts](scripts)
- [docs/PERFORMANCE_SCALABILITY_ANALYSIS_2025.md](docs/PERFORMANCE_SCALABILITY_ANALYSIS_2025.md)

content.body:
Package goal: replace hard-coded visual decisions with a consistent design system and tighten accessibility across the hub and tools.

Why this package matters:
- [gui/common/styles.py](gui/common/styles.py) still uses literal colors and direct style strings, which makes theme evolution and contrast control harder.
- The startup dialogs and shared windows show a lot of repeated widget styling that would benefit from shared components and tokens.
- Accessibility should be treated as a first-class UI requirement, not a validation afterthought.

Implementation items:
- Move shared visual decisions into a token-based theme layer instead of embedding raw colors in widget styles.
- Standardize dialogs, window chrome, and action states so the hub and tools feel like one product.
- Improve keyboard navigation, focus states, and accessible naming for interactive controls.
- Add specific checks for contrast, scaling, and screen-reader-friendly flows in the UI test suite.

Representative files:
- [gui/common/styles.py](gui/common/styles.py)
- [gui/common](gui/common)
- [main.py](main.py)
- [gui](gui)

content.body:
Package goal: strengthen the app's security posture and reduce supply-chain and audit gaps.

Why this package matters:
- [requirements.txt](requirements.txt) carries many security-sensitive packages and overlapping libraries that need a clear policy.
- Startup and tool execution paths handle file operations, authentication, encryption, and system integration, but the audit story is not yet unified.
- Security-related modules should share one approach for logging, policy checks, and traceability.

Implementation items:
- Add a centralized audit trail for file, configuration, and security operations with consistent metadata.
- Review dependency overlap and pin or rationalize security-critical packages, especially crypto, TLS, SSH, and archive libraries.
- Add automated vulnerability scanning to the validation pipeline.
- Normalize security-sensitive error handling so exceptions are auditable without leaking sensitive data.

Representative files:
- [requirements.txt](requirements.txt)
- [core/error_handler.py](core/error_handler.py)
- [src/core](src/core)
- [src/tools/security](src/tools/security)

content.body:
Package goal: break the largest orchestration surfaces into smaller, testable modules and standardize how tools register and launch.

Why this package matters:
- [main.py](main.py) performs startup orchestration, database bootstrapping, interface selection, and feature detection in one place.
- The exploration notes identified large modules such as the multi-pane explorer, migration manager, and database manager as the highest maintainability risk.
- Tool launch behavior is inconsistent across the app, which makes future tool additions and lifecycle testing harder.

Implementation items:
- Split monolithic orchestration modules into smaller boundaries with clear ownership and no behavior drift.
- Introduce a shared tool registry and a minimal tool lifecycle interface so launch, configure, and teardown follow one pattern.
- Add an explicit application state façade so config, preferences, theme, and logging dependencies are initialized in a predictable order.
- Keep compatibility adapters in place during the transition so existing tools do not break.

Representative files:
- [main.py](main.py)
- [gui/common](gui/common)
- [core](core)
- [src](src)
